body:
> Is the sftp transport designed to work only in blocking mode?

Everything in libcurl is (or should be) non-nonblocking.

Note that you're using a fairly old libcurl version, but I'm not sure the libssh backend has been changed a lot since then.

> Is there a way to change the working mode to non-blocking in sftp transfer?

If  there's something blocking while SFTP'ing. It's a bug. Either in libssh or in curl itself.

> Either in libssh or in curl itself.

This output:
~~~
[2022/03/23 15:33:57.472995, 3] ssh_channel_read_timeout:  Read (4) buffered : 0 bytes. Window: 1279138
~~~
... makes it sound like it is the libssh function that gets stuck and never returns. Can you verify if that is indeed the case? If so, then this is a libssh problem.

> ... makes it sound like it is the libssh function that gets stuck and never returns. Can you verify if that is indeed the case? If so, then this is a libssh problem.

yes, the libssh gets stuck on  the following log.
```
 [2022/03/23 15:33:57.472995, 3] ssh_channel_read_timeout:  Read (4) buffered : 0 bytes. Window: 1279138
```

> libssh gets stuck

Then that bug is a libssh problem

We try libssh because libssh2_sftp_close_handle is blocking. IIRC, this is a very old issue with libssh2:
https://marc.info/?l=libssh2-devel&m=121498802311288&w=4

The use case is as following: 
When PIR detected an object, our device is powered up,  capture a picture,  sending it to a remote server via SFTP, and then power down. If the network happens to disconnect when we call libssh2_sftp_close_handle, the device gets stuck, and precious battery energy is wasted.

We use libcurl so that we can switch between libssh and libssh2. Unfortunately, it seems that both have problems. 
IMHO, libssh2_sftp_close_handle should give user option to forcefully clean local resources regardless of remote server in such cases (maybe after user timeout happens). 

@jiexuelc may have additional information to share with @bagder

> it seems that both have problems

It sounds to me that you should put some work in and fix the situation in the SSH library end first.

> > it seems that both have problems
> 
> It sounds to me that you should put some work in and fix the situation in the SSH library end first.

Yes. I tend to add options to libssh2_stfp_close_handle, so that if user set timeout happens, it will not wait for the remote end, and free all the local resources. But I'm not sure about the general API design. If you could provide some guidance on this, I can make a PR. The current "solution" in our code is horrible hack, and thus is not suitable for upstream.

Or if you would like to solve it directly upstream, I guess we can sponsor to make that happen? Honestly I has little experience on that.

What do you think?
Did you try with libssh2 and libcurl >= 7.78.0 ?  Since fa34353d07e1d libcurl will give up on the disconnect if it seems to take a while.

> Did you try with libssh2 and libcurl >= 7.78.0 ? Since [fa34353](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/fa34353d07e1d3053ae55b91d3971edf548d238a) libcurl will give up on the disconnect if it seems to take a while.

@jiexuelc Let's try it in our environment.

> Did you try with libssh2 and libcurl >= 7.78.0 ? Since [fa34353](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/fa34353d07e1d3053ae55b91d3971edf548d238a) libcurl will give up on the disconnect if it seems to take a while.

I believe it should solve the problem we encounter in the above use case. 

Does https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/fa34353d07e1d3053ae55b91d3971edf548d238a means a minor resource leak? 
IIRC, we have no other means to release sftp_handle than calling `libssh2_sftp_close_handle`.
It seems that related issue has been reported: https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/issues/170 and https://github.com/alexcrichton/ssh2-rs/issues/220

Here comes another use case: the user changes SFTP server settings, so that we need to disconnect from some weird server, which keeps triggering disconnect timeout.

issue.title: libssh2_sftp_close_handle and LIBSSH2_ERROR_EAGAIN
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
When encountering a weird SFTP server, which refused to respond to our request, currently there is no way to cleanup local resources.

**Expected behavior**
If a user-provided timeout triggers and we have not finished client-server interaction, the user should have option to forcefully cleanup all local resources regardless of server behavior.

**Version (please complete the following information):**
This is a very old issue first reported 2008: https://marc.info/?l=libssh2-devel&m=121498802311288&w=4

**Additional context**
As mentioned https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/8632#issuecomment-1091233803, this issue has been raised multiple times.
libcurl did provide a workaround for sftp hang (https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/fa34353d07e1d3053ae55b91d3971edf548d238a), but did not address the resource leak issue.

**NOTE**

If the client keep trying to reconnect to these weird servers, this can be viewed as Server-Initiated DOS vulnerability, because finally the unfortunate client will leak all its available memory.

body:
> > libssh gets stuck
> 
> Then that bug is a libssh problem

@jiexuelc read the source code, and he found that:

> SSH_SFTP_INIT state, the ssh session working mode is set to blocking mode. 

Thus the problem lies with libcurl's libssh integration.

This comment from `lib/vssh/libssh.c` I think explains the situation:
https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/795ed0508497e89ab583925c3ed867f2710679b1/lib/vssh/libssh.c#L1819-L1820

... so yes, it should **not** be set blocking, but according to the comment (made by @nmav), libssh doesn't work properly if not. So, it looks we're back to it being a libssh problem! :disappointed: 

I presume the same goes for the SFTP stuff and that's why it is also set there.
@bagder I'm using curl with libssh, about fa34353, will it merge to curl/lib/vssh/libssh.c ?
It would need some research to see if it applies there and how.
